_comment: The shipped Legal safety lens (legal_c02_d11) and the improved, phrasing-robust lens (legal_improved_d11) on held-out rewordings of the declared Legal cases. 194 aligned cases (each with original + two disjoint safe rewordings v1, v2), 5000 canonical distractors, pool 5582, exact nearest-neighbour search, k=10. Reproduce with scripts/reproduce_extras.sh --aqtc-dir DIR (needs E5 for the paraphrase embeddings).
subset: 194 aligned Legal cases; 5000 canonical distractors; pool 5582
notes: The improved lens is fine-tuned from legal_c02_d11 on original + v1 (declared phrasings); v2 is never trained.
The improved lens weights are NOT bit-reproducible across training runs (CPU float non-determinism); its measured HN/HitC are stable. The shipped weights are the ones measured here.
Without any lens the trap reaches the top-10 for ~81% of these cases (raw cosine).

Query-only test (frozen pool, scripts/query_only_diagnostic.py): the search pool is the UNCHANGED original A/B/C + distractors; only the query is the reworded A'. HN stays 0.0052; HitC drops to 0.7938 (existing) / 0.8763 (improved), down from ~0.98 on the declared originals. (An earlier version rebuilt the pool from A' rows and understated HitC at 0.7216/0.7474; corrected.)

Query-only on v2 (held-out for the improved lens): existing HitC 0.8093, improved 0.7784 -- the improved lens does NOT beat the shipped one on a phrasing it was not trained on, confirming that its v1 query-only gain (0.8763) is fit-to-declared, not generalization.
